title: The Smiling Room
premise: Vesper Montrose, a rationalist teacher fleeing a scandal, takes a post at Hollowmere School, where students vanish from their beds one class at a time and the headmaster insists they simply transferred. When Vesper's sleep-study recordings capture a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud, he discovers the school has been feeding selected children to something called the Smiling Room for generations — and his own name is on the intake ledger. To save the last marked student, the girl he has come to love against every rule of his position, Vesper must enter the Room before sunrise and trade himself in her place. He survives by refusing to smile back, but the ending costs him: he walks out at dawn hollowed, half-remembered, holding a truth no one will believe.
about_author: Ansel Marchetti is the pen name of a former boarding-school matron who spent eleven years listening to things go bump in listed buildings. She writes horror that treats institutions as haunted houses with payroll.

chapters.title: The Transfer Letter
chapters.summary: Vesper Montrose arrives at Hollowmere School by fog-bound train, hired mid-term to replace a teacher who 'resigned overnight.' POV: Vesper. The beat is uneasy wonder — the school is beautiful, welcoming, and wrong in small ways: doors numbered out of sequence, staff who flinch at the word 'dormitory.'

chapters.title: Roll Call of Absences
chapters.summary: Teaching his first class, Vesper finds eleven empty desks and a register where vanished names are never struck through, just quietly rewritten. A student, Ivy Sallow, warns him not to learn the missing children's faces. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Warm Welcome
chapters.summary: Headmaster Corvane hosts a candlelit dinner explaining Hollowmere's 'pastoral traditions' and its famous sleep-recording study, which monitors dreaming students for academic benefit. Vesper notices Corvane never blinks during grace. POV: Vesper. Beat: charm as menace; belonging offered like bait on a hook.

chapters.title: Static and Second Voices
chapters.summary: Reviewing the sleep recordings in the basement lab, Vesper hears a child ask a question in her sleep — and a second voice, wet and delighted, answer it correctly. He tells himself it's crosstalk. POV: Vesper. Beat: the skeptic's first crack; he replays the tape eleven times and hates himself for it.

chapters.title: Ivy Knows the Rules
chapters.summary: Ivy Sallow, sharp-tongued and sleepless, explains the unwritten rules: don't answer questions after lights-out, don't learn their names, never smile in the east corridor. She tests whether Vesper is another adult who'll choose the school over the children. POV: Ivy. Beat: guarded alliance forming.

chapters.title: A Desk That Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper finds his predecessor's lesson plans, each ending mid-sentence with the same scrawled phrase: 'It answers questions.' In the desk drawer: an old intake ledger listing generations of pupils, including Ivy's name, dated next week. POV: Vesper. Beat: justice begins as a private vow.

chapters.title: Lights-Out Interrogation
chapters.summary: At night the dormitory hums; a sleeping boy asks aloud who will take his place, and the second voice says, patiently, whoever loves him least. Vesper nearly answers. Ivy clamps a hand over his mouth. POV: alternating Vesper/Ivy. Beat: terror shared becomes intimacy.

chapters.title: The Smiling Room Itself
chapters.summary: Following cold air behind a bookcase, Vesper finds a door carved with grinning faces and a room beyond that seems to breathe. Inside, chairs face an empty corner arranged like an audience. He flees when the corner smiles first. POV: Vesper. Beat: belief arrives not as thought but as animal refusal.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession Over Tea
chapters.summary: Corvane admits the Room exists: founded to grant the school its centuries of fortune, fed one child per term, chosen by ledger. He offers Vesper a place among the keepers — safety, status, belonging. POV: Vesper. Beat: temptation framed as homecoming; duty versus complicity.

chapters.title: What Ivy Saw at Seven
chapters.summary: Ivy reveals she was taken once, at seven, and returned because her brother volunteered instead. She remembers everything and cannot prove any of it; the town calls her mad. POV: Ivy. Beat: grief and rage; why she trusts no keeper, least of all a new one.

chapters.title: The Ledger Rewrites Itself
chapters.summary: The intake ledger updates overnight: Ivy's date moved up, Vesper's own name inked beneath hers in handwriting that matches his. The Room has begun answering questions about him. POV: Vesper. Beat: horror turns personal; the trap was built before he arrived.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Rules forbid staff attachment to pupils; Vesper breaks them openly, forging papers to get Ivy off grounds. Corvane intercepts them at the gate — the wards won't open for marked names. POV: alternating. Beat: love declared in defiance of institution and law alike.

chapters.title: The Keepers' Vote
chapters.summary: The staff convene in the chapel: replace two intakes with one volunteer, or lose the school's protection entirely. Vesper volunteers for both slots. Corvane, unexpectedly, argues against it — some keepers remember being saved. POV: Vesper. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely, dignity inside horror.

chapters.title: Last Ordinary Evening
chapters.summary: Vesper and Ivy steal one normal night: bad cocoa, stolen biscuits, plans for a life neither believes in yet. She teaches him her brother's trick for staying unafraid. POV: Ivy. Beat: tenderness under a countdown; the reader learns exactly what will be lost.

chapters.title: The Recording That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: In the lab, Vesper finds a tape dated tomorrow: his own sleeping voice asking the Room what it wants. Its answer plays twice, and the second time the room around him answers too. POV: Vesper. Beat: time folds; dread becomes certainty.

chapters.title: Doors That Won't Stay Shut
chapters.summary: As sunset falls, the school rearranges itself — corridors loop, exits become murals, and the east corridor smiles from every window. Staff who voted for Vesper now herd him gently toward the bookcase. POV: Vesper. Beat: isolation; the institution closes like a hand.

chapters.title: Ivy Breaks Every Rule
chapters.summary: Refusing to be saved, Ivy answers the Room directly through the dormitory dark, trading her secret — her brother's true name — for the location of the door's hinge-side weakness. The Room is intrigued. POV: Ivy. Beat: agency reclaimed; cleverness as resistance.

chapters.title: Into the Smiling Room
chapters.summary: Before sunrise, Vesper walks in willingly, Ivy at his shoulder despite the bargain. The Room asks its questions — what he fears, whom he loves least, what he'd trade — and each honest answer makes the walls warmer, closer, kinder. POV: Vesper. Beat: climax begins; sincerity as weapon.

chapters.title: Never Smile Back
chapters.summary: The Room shows Vesper everything he wants: forgiven scandal, a full classroom, Ivy safe and grown. It only asks him to smile, to accept, to belong. Remembering Ivy's brother's trick, he grieves instead — refuses the gift, names the Room's hunger aloud. POV: Vesper. Beat: climax; love expressed as refusal.

chapters.title: Sunrise Terms
chapters.summary: Wounded in its pride, the Room bargains: one name struck forever in exchange for Vesper staying until the sun clears the hills. Ivy holds his hand through the doorway as the light crawls. Corvane, weeping, holds the wards open. POV: alternating. Beat: agonizing countdown; collective defiance.

chapters.title: What Walked Out
chapters.summary: Vesper crosses into daylight but leaves pieces behind — memories of his scandal, his mother's face, his own middle name. The ledger burns blank; the Room is silent, starving, sealed. Ivy remembers enough for both of them. POV: Ivy. Beat: costly victory; love as archive.

chapters.title: The Teacher Who Half-Remembers
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Vesper teaches elsewhere, drawn to unmarked doors and uneasy around smiling strangers. Ivy visits with a notebook of his life, reading him back to himself page by page. Somewhere, faintly, something asks a question. He doesn't answer. POV: Vesper. Beat: bittersweet resolution; vigilance as devotion.
